title: Template-driven deployment harmonizer for environment constraints
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
We need a convergent service (Deployment Harmonizer) that compiles high-level rollout plans (canary, A/B, shadow, auto-rollback) into environment-aware manifests for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. The harmonizer enforces config parity where possible and emits explicit constraints/exceptions when platform differences require divergence. This ticket covers the design, prototype, validation, and initial integrations with SLO/rollback controllers and the Console preview UI.

Why this work:
- Current rollout definitions are free-form and manual changes slip through when promoting between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (different networking, RBAC, KMS, and autoscale semantics).
- We still see incidents where private deployments deploy unsupported feature flags or invalid autoscale configs because there is no pre-validation against environment constraints.
- A single translation layer reduces developer cognitive load and lowers customer incident risk during promotion / rollouts.

Scope / Goals:
1) Define a compact "environment constraint template" format (YAML/JSON Schema) that captures the key differences (eg. max burst scale, VLAN-only endpoints, KMS policy required, disabled cross-region failover).
2) Implement Deployment Harmonizer service (stateless translator + validator) that:
   - Inputs: high-level rollout policy (percentages, stages, traffic routing rules, rollback triggers).
   - Outputs: per-environment rollout manifests and a normalized diff report.
   - Provides a dry-run validation API and a human-readable console preview.
3) Integrate with SLO-aware traffic controller (ENG-8451) for rollback trigger translation and with rollout orchestration hooks (canary windows, shadow probes).
4) Surface explicit warnings for environment exceptions and produce recommended mitigations (eg. degrade to A/B split instead of shadow if private node count too low).

Decisions made so far:
- Policy-first (declarative) approach: we will treat the harmonizer as a translator for a single source-of-truth rollout policy rather than embedding environment logic into each client. This avoids divergence across SDKs.
- Templates will be JSON Schema-compatible so we can reuse existing validation tooling and show clear error messages.
- Harmonizer will be implemented as a lightweight service in the orchestration plane (not a CRD) to avoid exposing cluster-level changes to customers on Private installs.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Strict parity vs pragmatic exceptions: enforcing strict parity reduces surprises but may block valid private customers who require relaxation. We will support "opt-in relaxations" via signed justification metadata stored in the release record.
- Service vs CRD: service centralizes logic and allows versioned compatibility checks but adds another runtime dependency for Private installs. We chose service to enable consistent behavior across deployment modes.
- Where to store templates: initial plan is to keep canonical templates in the control plane (hosted repo) and provide an exportable bundle for Private customers.

Progress updates / artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/Template+Harmonizer+Design (internal) -- first draft complete.
- Prototype translator: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/462 (draft) implementing schema compile + dry-run translation for a simple canary plan.
- Unit tests: 24/36 passing in prototype (missing edge cases for shadow traffic rerouting).
- Spike: validated private environment where KMS-required flag blocks rollout; added a mitigation suggestion flow.

Review feedback received:
- PM (Lena Park): prefer clearer UX for "opt-in relaxations" with audit trail and approver flow.
- Security: require encryption of exported template bundles; add security_review_required tag.
- Design: Console preview should show a per-stage impact matrix (latency, cost, capacity) -- not just a textual diff.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harmonizer service accepts a canonical rollout policy and produces validated per-environment manifests for Hosted/Dedicated/Private without errors for the happy path.
- Dry-run API returns human-readable diffs and structured warnings for any constraint violations.
- Integration test with ENG-8451 SLO controller shows rollback triggers correctly translated for canary stage.
- Console preview in Console-2025.11 shows harmonized plan and allow a user to "approve with mitigation".

Implementation plan (next steps):
- Week 1: Finish JSON Schema templates for common rollout patterns (canary, A/B, shadow, promote). Update design doc with template reference.
- Week 2: Merge prototype PR after addressing shadow rerouting edge cases; add exhaustive unit tests.
- Week 3: Integrate dry-run API into Console preview and add e2e test against a dedicated sandbox.
- Week 4: Security review and export bundle encryption; create runbook for Private installs.

Follow-ups and subsequent work:
- Add automatic rollback policy suggestions based on historical regressions and platform capacity.
- Build migration tool to convert existing rollouts into harmonizer-compliant policies.
- Add telemetry for "exception usage" to inform product decisions.

Known dependencies / blockers:
- ENG-8451 (SLO-aware traffic controller) -- need final API for rollback events.
- Console feature branch console-2025.11 for preview UI.
- Security sign-off for template bundle export.

Acceptance test links / dashboards:
- Canary experiment dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/canary-experiments-overview
- E2E test run for prototype: https://buildkite.com/redwood/orchestrator-builds/collections/33177

Notes for reviewers:
- Please review the JSON Schema examples in the design doc and the PR. Focus on whether the template captures necessary constraints without being overly prescriptive.
- PM asked for a UX flow for approvals; design sketches are in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Hx-TemplateHarmonizer

Next milestones (short):
- 2025-11-21: Merge translator PR and enable dry-run in staging.
- 2025-11-28: Console preview + initial QA.
- 2025-12-05: Release harmonizer alpha behind feature flag for internal teams.

Post-release metrics to track:
- Reduction in private->hosted rollout mismatch incidents (target: -60% in first 3 months).
- Number of "opt-in relaxations" and time to approval.
- False positive warnings from template validation (target < 5%).
